newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Judge fines Czech party for spying allegations.
newsitem.headline: Judge fines Czech party for spying allegations.

text.p: A Prague judge ruled on Monday that the opposition Social Democratic Party must pay the former head of the Czech secret service one million crowns ($35,000) for alleging agents under his direction had spied on the party, CTK news agency said.

It said the ruling called for the party to pay former Security Information Service (BIS) director, Stanislav Devaty, for damages stemming from the unfounded allegations made by Social Democrat chairman Milos Zeman last November. The allegations became a political football in the run-up to Senate elections that month.

Zeman said he had evidence that the BIS and the interior ministry had created a group to spy on Social Democrat functionaries, but lawyers for Devaty said that the evidence was inconclusive and that the allegations damaged the head of the BIS himself.
A parliamentary commission has rejected Zeman's charges.

Counsel for the Social Democratic Party argued that Zeman's allegations were directed at the BIS in general, and not specifically at Devaty. Party officials said after the ruling that the judge's decision in favour of Devaty was politically motivated.

Devaty, a former member of Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS), quit the BIS in November after allegations by the chairman of a junior partner in the ruling coalition, Josef Lux, that BIS agents had spied on him.

The Social Democrat allegations, which followed those of Lux, became a source of heated confrontations between members of the ODS and the Social Democrats on the eve of Senate elections in which the ruling coalition won a solid majority. ($ = 28.34 Czech Crowns)
